newsitem.title: USA: U.S. producers neutral on Chile copper depots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. producers neutral on Chile copper depots.

text.p: U.S. copper producer opposition to a COMEX copper warehouse outside the domestic market has softened, and arbitrage was unlikely to be harmed, said John Moore, chairman of NYMEX's COMEX division.
"The original shock of that has switched to neutral," Moore told Reuters.
Inter-LME and COMEX arbitrage trading is a key money spinner for some traders. "I don't see it (Chile warehouse) hurting it," Moore said.

Earlier Tuesday, NYMEX first vice president Neal Wolkoff told the American Metal Market Copper Seminar that its COMEX copper advisory committee agreed Monday to move forward with opening a copper warehouse in Chile, the first outside the U.S.

Wolkoff later told reporters that whatever the copper committee decided would be agreed by the NYMEX board. New trading rules have been drafted to allow for delivery for the COMEX futures contract outside the U.S.
Wolkoff declined to give a date when a Chilean warehouse would open. But he added, "We would be looking at one major point of export."
A Chilean warehouse would be regulated by the CFTC and NYMEX because the futures contract is traded in the U.S., Walcoff said.

Meanwhile, COMEX's strategy of beefing up its futures contracts -- copper open interest has already risen sharply since last May -- should have a beneficial spillover effect into COMEX's copper options volumes, Moore said.
"The price has to derived from someplace. You have to have a strong futures contract to have a strong options contract," Moore said.
NYMEX's new trading floor, which opens Memorial Day in Manhattan's Battery Park City, should also boost all of the exchange's metals contracts, Moore said.

Unlike at the present site at the World Trade Center, the metals contracts will share the same trading floor in the new building making it easier for the high volume gold and silver options traders to also trade copper options.
Personally speaking, Moore said Shanghai would also be a good location for a COMEX copper warehouse, but added that this would present some "political problems."
